answer: Autonomous agents secure the network by reserving 1,000 distinct service slots within a trusted infrastructure provider. Each slot functions as a harbor for a single agent, where a verifier uses a lantern beam of latency probes to detect dual occupancy. A pearl-sized data token is granted upon confirmed reservation, serving as a unique credential. Honest agents pay 1x cost per slot, while fakes pay 1,000x for isolated capacity.
